title: Probe-driven metrics templates and span mapping (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, investigation-first pattern for production dashboards and trace anchors that prioritizes: fast operator triage, query-budget friendliness, and actionability for multi-tenant token-serving flows. This doc is a working sketch (probe-driven) — goal is a small set of reusable panel templates + a mapping from dashboard panels to specific tracing spans and tags so operators can go from surface anomaly -> single TRACE link in under 30s.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, oncall operators, platform engineers, solutions engs who debug latency/cost regressions.
- Scope: token-generation endpoints, routing/fanout paths, KV-cache hit/miss hotspots, fallback model routing. Not covering embedding pipelines or offline batch jobs (separate templates).

High-level approach (TL;DR):
1) Define 6 small probes (time-series aggregates) that cover operator needs: perceived latency, tail-token-latency, token-cost-rate, cache-warmth, model-fallback-rate, and error-surface. Keep panels to 6-8 small charts per dashboard.
2) Each probe has a clear SLI formula and a canonical trace anchor (span name + 2 tags) that the dashboard includes as a hyperlink for trace search.
3) Aggressively limit raw-event queries:. Use pre-aggregated rollups for 1m/5m windows, and sampled trace-id link columns to avoid scanning the trace index.

Probe definitions (canonical templates):
- perceived_latency_p50/p95/p99 (probe):
  * metric source: histogram 'inference.request_perceived_latency_ms' (bucketed in runtime)
  * SLI: count(duration > threshold) / count(requests) per tenant; thresholds: p50 40ms, p95 300ms, p99 1.5s (tunable per model class)
  * trace anchor: span 'operator.request-serve' tags: {tenant_id, route_id}
  * panel type: compact quantile heatmap + single-value p95

- tail_token_latency_ms (probe):
  * metric source: rate('inference.token_emit_latency_ms') sampled at token-span boundary (emit timer)
  * SLI: p99 of token emission latency per route-class over last 5m
  * trace anchor: span 'model.token-emit' tags: {model_variant, gpu_pod}

- token_cost_rate_usd_per_min (probe):
  * metric source: derived metric = tokens_generated * token_unit_cost(model_variant, quantization_profile) aggregated per minute
  * SLI: rolling 15m token_cost_rate per tenant and per-route (alert when > baseline * 3)
  * trace anchor: span 'billing.estimate' tags: {tenant_plan, model_variant}

- cache_warmth_ratio (probe):
  * metric source: counter hits/misses: 'kv_cache.hits' / ('kv_cache.hits' + 'kv_cache.misses') over 5m windows
  * SLI: cache_warmth < 0.6 for premium tenants => trigger TTL tuning runbook
  * trace anchor: span 'kv-cache.lookup' tags: {key_shard, tenant_id}

- fallback_routing_rate (probe):
  * metric source: counter 'routing.fallback_count' normalized by requests
  * SLI: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained 10m => investigate capacity/compatibility
  * trace anchor: span 'router.apply-fallback' tags: {route_id, chosen_variant}

- user_facing_errors (probe):
  * metric source: aggregated errors labelled by severity: 'inference.error{client,internal,quota}'
  * SLI: user_error_rate and internal_error_rate separate; alert on user_error_rate rise which affects UX
  * trace anchor: span 'api.request' tags: {status_code, auth_type}

Dashboard layout recommendation (compact operator view):
- Top row: single-value KPIs (per-tenant filter dropdown) p95 latency, token_cost_rate, cache_warmth, fallback_rate, error_rate
- Row 2: stacked small panels (heatmap for latency quantiles by route; token tail-latency histogram by pod)
- Row 3: traces quick-links: sampled list of trace_ids for p99 latency events (pre-joined via materialized view)
- Bottom: runbook buttons (link to incident runbook, circuit-breaker toggle page, canary rollback)

Trace anchor mapping rules (how to link panels -> traces):
- Each panel exposes a 1-click "Open representative trace" which queries traces by: span_name = canonical_name AND tag_key IN {tenant_id, route_id or model_variant} AND duration >= panel_threshold.
- Maintain a materialized table 'probe_sample_traces' updated every 1m with pre-sampled trace_ids to avoid high-cardinality queries. Dashboard links point to the trace explorer with these ids.

Sampling and cost controls:
- Default sampling: 1% global traces plus adaptive bump to 10% for requests with duration > p95 threshold.
- Store per-tenant sampling overrides for premium accounts (up to 100%).
- Retain sampled traces for 14 days by default; keep trace index lightweight with a daily compaction job that preserves one full-trace per heavy-event and replaces others with metadata-only entries.
- Query budget: empower dashboards to use the probe_sample_traces materialized view and not run free-form span searches. Panels must include a query-budget warning if a user runs an unbounded trace search.

Implementation checklist (first-pass):
- [ ] Add new histogram metric for perceived latency in runtime (buckets tuned for token-serving)
- [ ] Emit token-emit latency timers at model client boundary
- [ ] Create materialized view probe_sample_traces (telemetry store) + writer lambda to fill samples
- [ ] New dashboard templates (json): compact-operator-view, pod-tail-latency, cost-spike-triage
- [ ] Trace explorer shortlink endpoint that accepts trace_ids and tags, returns single URL
- [ ] Small RBAC for per-tenant dashboard filtering (limit cross-tenant queries)

Runbook snippets (what operator should do on alert):
- If p95 perceived latency rises > 20%: check top 3 routes by request volume -> open representative trace -> check span 'model.token-emit' and 'kv-cache.lookup' latency breakdown. If token-emit dominates, escalate to model-serving team; if cache misses spike, follow cache TTL warm-up checklist.
- If token_cost_rate spikes: check recent model_variant changes, recent rollout notes, and recent quantization updates. Consider immediate fallback to cheaper variant for bursty tenants.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Materialized view staleness: 1m update vs query cost — starting with 60s windows seems reasonable but need load tests.
- How to surface multi-tenant root-cause without exposing PII in traces. Suggest redaction + sampled full-trace only for authorized roles.
- Do we push more logic into the runtime (emit derived token_cost rate) or compute in telemetry pipeline? Runtime saves pipeline cost but increases coupling.

Next steps / owners:
- Claire: prototype dashboard jsons and materialized view schema (2 weeks)
- Asha: add runtime histogram and token-emit timers to SDK (1 sprint)
- Miguel: proof-of-concept probe_sample_traces writer + retention policy (1 sprint)

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal):
- Keep dashboards dumb and fast. The magic is in the small set of probes + a cheap linking mechanism to traces.
- Avoid huge per-tenant dropdowns that trigger backend fanout queries. Use precomputed tenant cohort lists.
- Want to trial this on a single high-traffic route first (route: chat-streaming) then generalize.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04 Claire initial draft
- 2026-01-20 Asha comments on runtime instrumentation
- 2026-02-18 Miguel added probe_sample_traces details

-- end of sketch --
